salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 32-year-old woman
1-year history of swelling
Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration yielded no fluid
Complex and septated mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
Mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter

shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of a slow-growing, subcutaneous mass with overlying skin erythema

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: common benign tumor that can present as a slow-growing, subcutaneous mass

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst

raw.rationale: The complex and septated mass, along with the location near the gluteal cleft and adherence to subcutaneous fat, is consistent with an epidermoid cyst, which is a type of inclusion cyst that can present as a slow-growing, painless mass.

rejected.label: Pilomatricoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a firm, rock-hard nodule, often with overlying skin changes, which does not match the description of the mass in this case

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Usually a soft, mobile, and well-circumscribed mass, which does not fit the complex and septated nature of the mass described

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: A rare skin cancer that typically presents as a firm, painless nodule or plaque, often with a history of slow growth, but the description of the mass and its location does not strongly suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Inclusion cyst
rejected.why: While this is a broad category that includes epidermoid cysts, the term is too general and 'Epidermoid cyst' is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the key facts
